Kukeziv Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Lviv Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Kukeziv has an unusually layered religious history: Karaites — a Jewish sect that rejects rabbinic tradition — settled here in 1692 under a grant from Polish King Jan Sobieski III, and the 17th-century Karaite writer Mordechai Kukizov lived in the town; after 1831, the Karaite community relocated to Galich. Mainstream Jews then settled in Kukeziv during the late 19th and early 20th centuries, only to be deported to the ghetto in Novyy Yarychiv and executed there following the Nazi occupation of 1941. The cemetery itself, presumably in use until 1831, is thought to have been demolished in the 1960s, its gravestones reportedly used, according to local testimony, to help build the road to Moscow.
